subject.title: fix(codex): scoped tool allowlist blocks the user MCP servers it explicitly allows

question: Should scoped Codex tool allowlists expose matching configured static MCP servers as OpenClaw dynamic tools, with OpenClaw-owned naming and approvals, instead of native Codex MCP servers?
rationale: The patch repairs lost access without granting wildcard native shell/file tools, but it deliberately moves the user-visible authorization and presentation boundary for scoped turns.

options.title: Approve dynamic scoped MCP
options.body: Adopt the bridge as the canonical scoped-turn path after direct Codex contract review confirms its tool and approval semantics.

options.title: Preserve native ownership
options.body: Require a Codex-native per-tool MCP projection instead, accepting the additional protocol and catalog work needed to retain Codex naming and approvals.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers do not want scoped and unrestricted turns to use different MCP ownership models.

recommendation.title: Approve dynamic scoped MCP
recommendation.body: Adopt the bridge as the canonical scoped-turn path after direct Codex contract review confirms its tool and approval semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier proposal addressed the same Codex/MCP ownership boundary, though current-main ownership remains uncertain.
